{"candidate_rtl":"module decoder_8bit
 #(
    parameter N = 8
) (
    input [N-1:0] in,
    output reg [(1<<N)-1:0] out
);
    wire [15:0] low_decode;
    wire [15:0] high_decode;
    wire [255:0] decoded;

    assign low_decode  = 16'b1 << in[3:0];
    assign high_decode = 16'b1 << in[7:4];

    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < 256; i = i + 1) begin : gen_decode
            assign decoded[i] = low_decode[i % 16] & high_decode[i / 16];
        end
    endgenerate

    always @(*) begin
        out = decoded;
    end
endmodule","bottleneck":"The original implementation is synthesized as a wide decoder with shared product terms, and its critical path includes input buffering, a predecode term, and a final output combine gate. The explicit two-level 4-bit predecode preserves sharing while limiting each output to one final two-input combine.","rewrite":"Split the 8-bit input into upper and lower nibbles, decode each nibble into a 16-bit one-hot vector, and form each of the 256 outputs as the conjunction of one upper and one lower predecode term.","expected_timing_gain":"Expected modest improvement or equivalent timing, with the critical path reduced to nibble predecode plus one final AND-level combine. The exact gain depends on ABC factoring and SKY130HD cell selection.","area_or_other_cost":"Uses two shared 16-way predecoders and 256 explicit two-input combine terms. Area is expected to remain near the baseline and within the stated cap; no sequential, clock, storage, or external dependencies are introduced.","functional_boundaries":"For N=8, decoded[i] is asserted exactly when in equals i, including all 256 arbitrary input values. Output width, unsigned behavior, truncation behavior, default combinational behavior, module name, ports, and parameter declaration are retained."}
